title: Sunk capacity rebalance simulator
summary: Working simulator + prototype spreadsheet to model "sunk" reserved GPU capacity and practical rebalancing levers. Focus is on short-duration credit swaps, intra-pool reallocation, and measured overcommit windows to reduce marginal unit cost while preserving SLA headroom.
objectives: (1) Quantify near-term cashflow savings from rebalancing unused reserved GPUs across workloads; (2) Provide parametric knobs (rebalance window, burst credit %, per-workload priority weight) for product ops to simulate outcomes; (3) Produce prioritized recommendations that are low friction to experiment with on Dedicated contracts.
assumptions: All cost numbers are USD. Reserved GPU unit = 1xV100-equivalent billing slot for modeling purposes. Baseline committed pool price = $9.50 / GPU-hour (blended). On-demand price assumed $22 / GPU-hour. SLA headroom requirement defaults to 15% of peak demand; can be toggled. Short-duration credits cost equal to 60% of on-demand hourly price when purchased from marketplace. Workload demand traces are weekly-aggregated and smoothed with a 7-day moving average.
spreadsheet_snapshot_sample:
SAMPLE OUTPUT (weekly):
Total committed GPU-hours: 4000
Idle committed hours (estimated): 860 (21.5%)
Projected short-duration credit spend to cover peaks: $6,120
Rebalance savings (first 12 weeks): $48,750
Net savings after transition friction: $36,500 (est)
scenarios: Scenario A - Conservative: allow rebalancing for pools with >25% idle for 4 consecutive weeks; no overcommit; only intra-contract reassignments
Scenario B - Credit-augmented: sell short-term credits into marketplace for low-util workloads and buy credits for peak windows; allow 10% transient overcommit
Scenario C - Aggressive overcommit: permit 25% overcommit with automatic fallback routing to hosted models; requires monitoring and fallback policy setup
Scenario D - Priority-preserving: rebalancing prioritized by priority_weight; protect top 2 workloads (by weight) from any reductions
formulas_and_notes:
Key formulas (human-readable):
- idle_hours = committed_hours - observed_used_hours
- effective_util = observed_used_hours / committed_hours * 100
- marginal_saving_per_hour_if_released = blended_commit_price - market_short_credit_price
- projected_cashflow_savings = sum(released_hours * marginal_saving_per_hour_if_released) - transition_costs
Notes: use 7-day MA of observed_used_hours to avoid reacting to single-day anomalies. When modeling overcommit, include expected fallback cost: fallback_cost = pct_fallback * on_demand_rate * fallback_hours.
sensitivity_highlights: Top sensitivities observed when running the simulator: (1) Market short-credit price swings (±20%) change 12-week savings by roughly ±35%. (2) SLA headroom threshold is leverageable: reducing headroom from 15% to 10% increases theoretical releasable capacity by ~12% but increases fallback risk. (3) Workload priority skew: if realtime-chat grows 15% above historical trace, half of projected savings evaporate due to protected headroom.
recommendations: Pilot Scenario B on two contracts with >30% idle historical windows (8–12 week experiment); instrument fallbacks and extra alerting
Introduce 'rebalancing windows' policy: weekly re-eval, min 3-week sustained idle to qualify for release
Build quick operator UI to flag candidate pools and simulate immediate P&L impact before operator approval
Negotiate optional short-term credit purchase rights in renewals (goal: cap marketplace price exposure)
Add automated guardrail: don’t release >40% of a pool in a single week; ramp released capacity over 3 weeks
